established: Following and muting are personal choices; the platform still ranks the feed. Earlier part2 already explains behavioral signals.
missing: Show the gap between a human intention and the consequence of ranking, so the chorus asks a motivated question.
options: Misread signal

I paused to disagree.
It read that pause as praise.
Now the same old quarrel
Fills the coming days.
A pause can mean disagreement, yet produce more of the same. Gives the next chorus a concrete inference to question. Fictional example, not a universal platform claim.
Different windows

We follow the same friend.
We sit here side by side.
Your screen shows her story.
Mine has pushed it aside.
Two people compare outcomes from the same followed source. Makes hidden selection visible through contrast, without repeating the definition of ranking.
Lost intention

Came to check on a friend.
A clip becomes a chain.
Half an hour later,
I forgot why I came.
Shows the human cost: recommendation momentum displaces the original social purpose. No new platform feature or workshop plot is assumed.

established: The person supplies a brief, corrects sales language, verifies facts and explicitly authorizes publication.
missing: Move from making a page to observing a real use problem and improving the artifact. The next verse then generalizes what to retain.
options: Visitor question

Someone asks, ‘Which door?’
The address wasn't clear.
Add the side-street entrance.
Now they know we're here.
A reader exposes missing practical information after publication; a specific revision makes the page more useful. New entrance detail is fictional and pending review.
Read aloud

Hear the page read back.
‘Click here’ tells me less.
Name the link ‘Directions.’
Now the words make sense.
An accessibility check reveals an unhelpful link label; repair meaning, not merely whether the link works. Distinct from the preceding technical link check.
Changed conditions

Rain moves us indoors.
The old page points outside.
Change the place we're meeting.
Keep the time beside.
A real-world change makes published information stale. Update only the changed fact, illustrating ongoing usefulness rather than a one-shot output.

established: Editable saved preferences, harness/tool rules, inspectable notes, bounded reach and model replacement already appear in parts1–3.
missing: Show a specific rule for handling accumulated context, which gives substance to the selected B chorus about thought shaping a harness.
options: Conflicting notes

An old note says ‘Keep short.’
Today I need detail.
Use the newer question.
Let the old rule yield.
Demonstrates precedence: a saved general preference must not defeat the current request. Adds conflict resolution, not another ownership or model-switch claim.
Relevant context

Notes from other work
Don't belong in here.
Bring the workshop folder.
Keep this purpose clear.
Demonstrates scope: retrieve context relevant to this task rather than mix every retained note. Does not repeat portability or permission.
Trace the answer

Where did that date come from?
Point me to the line.
Show the note behind it.
Then I'll know what to revise.
Demonstrates traceability from a claim back to its supporting note, so corrections target a source instead of guessing. More specific than merely viewing a list of notes.
